premise: I cashed out my $117,000 401(k) after 30 years as a hospital cafeteria worker to buy a vintage-bicycle restoration shop with my nephew, who promised in writing a 45% share and free tune-ups for my grandkids; when a transportation museum offered $620,000 for the restored 1890s penny-farthings and early roadsters, he forged a dissolution, sold the collection, and mailed me a $3,800 'spoke' check. I retrieved our signed agreement from inside the hollow seatpost of a 1937 Schwinn Autocycle we’d restored together, voided the sale, and now run 'Gear of Deceit Cycles,' where he trues wheels in a vest that says 'Spun Out of Trust' and every repair tag prints his fraud-docket number.
